questions.q: Why must human-centred design solutions keep adapting after launch?
options: Because people and their needs are dynamic and changing
questions.explain: Measure effectiveness against the original aims and keep improving.
questions.evidence: HCD recognizes that people and their needs are dynamic and changing, and so solutions must also adapt to changing needs.

options: A qualitative research method to solve problems with solutions that put customer needs ahead of a system's needs
A way to design attractive logos
questions.explain: It starts from people's real needs, not the organisation's processes.
questions.evidence: Human-centered design (HCD) is a qualitative research method that helps groups solve problems and seek solutions that prioritize customer needs over a system’s needs.

questions.q: How should you think of an HCD discovery?
options: As the final step of a project
As a straight line from start to finish
As a cycle, not a linear process
questions.explain: Each round of learning sends you back to refine questions.
questions.evidence: Think of HCD discovery as a cycle, instead of a linear process.

options: Letting the most senior person decide
Giving participants an active role in the life cycle of the work
Asking users to pay for the design
Designing alone, then presenting to users
questions.explain: Participants act as equals to the design team and leadership.
questions.evidence: Giving participants an active role in the life cycle of our work is sometimes called participatory design.

questions.q: What happens in the solution implementation step of the design process?
options: The final concept options are selected and carried through to completion
questions.explain: Implementation turns the chosen concept into finished designs.
questions.evidence: we are ready to select the final concept options and carry their application through to completion in producing the final design(s).

questions.q: In a design studio session, what should you remind participants about sketching?
options: Anyone can draw — artistic accuracy is not the goal
questions.explain: Quick, rough sketches let everyone contribute ideas.
questions.evidence: Remind them that anyone can draw and artistic accuracy is not the goal of the exercise.

questions.q: Why should you map a user's whole problem?
options: To find more users to charge
Because what you are working on is probably part of a bigger task users are trying to complete
questions.explain: Mapping shows how the journey is delivered today and where to improve it.
questions.evidence: This is because what they’re working on is probably part of a bigger task that users are trying to complete.

questions.q: Who are the creative thinkers, according to 'Words of Wisdom'?
options: Those who always pick option A
Those who invent solution C while everyone else argues between A and B
Those who copy the best existing answer
questions.explain: Creative and critical thinking work together.
questions.evidence: They are the ones who invent solution C when everyone else is still arguing between A and B.

questions.q: What must you do before committing to build anything?
options: Make prototypes to explore, share and test different designs
questions.explain: Prototypes are cheap ways to learn what works.
questions.evidence: You must make prototypes of your service to explore, share and test different designs before you commit to building anything.

questions.q: How should prototypes be, according to the 18F method?
options: Quick and painless to create — and even quicker to discard
questions.explain: Low-cost prototypes make it easy to throw away ideas that don't work.
questions.evidence: Prototypes should be quick and painless to create, and even more quick and painless to discard.
